question: Which ticketing platforms don't charge per-ticket fees?
answer:
Among the platforms reviewed on this site, these charge no fee of their own on each ticket sold:

  • Chobble Tickets: one flat price of £50/year or £5/month, or £25/year or £2.50/month for charities, community groups, artists and musicians, with every feature included.
  • tickts: a free plan with no commission, and paid plans of up to £690 a year for more features.
  • Event Schedule: a free plan capped at 25 paid tickets a month, then US$5 or US$15 a month.
  • Bookwhen: monthly plans priced by how many bookings you take.
  • Tessera Tickets: monthly plans that rise with yearly ticket volume.
  • Zeffy and Dandelion: no compulsory fee, with buyers asked for a voluntary contribution instead. Zeffy is only for registered nonprofits.
  • FooEvents and EventPrime: paid plugins for a WordPress site you run yourself.
  • SumUp Online Store: no platform fee, but each online payment costs 2.5%.

No per-ticket fee does not always mean a fixed price. Booking allowances and volume tiers can still raise the bill as sales grow, while the Chobble Tickets price stays the same at any volume. The provider directory can be filtered to platforms with no per-ticket fee.

question: How much does Eventbrite charge per ticket?
answer:
In the UK, Eventbrite charges 6.95% + £0.59 on each paid ticket, and that includes card processing. On a £15 ticket the fee is £1.63. Free events carry no fee. These figures were checked on 8 August 2026.

Chobble Tickets charges no fee per ticket. Managed hosting is £50/year or £5/month, and the organiser's Stripe account charges 1.5% + 20p per payment, which is about 43p on a £15 ticket. Selling £15 tickets one per order, the £50 is covered after about 42 tickets a year. The Eventbrite comparison covers the other differences.

question: What is the cheapest ticketing platform for small events?
answer:
For one small event, a short sales window usually costs least. One month of Chobble Tickets managed hosting costs £5, or £2.50 for charities, community groups, artists and musicians, with no per-ticket fee.

As an example, take 50 single-ticket orders at £10 sold within one month. On Chobble Tickets that costs £5 for hosting plus £17.50 in Stripe charges, which is £22.50 in total. The same sales on Eventbrite's UK pricing cost £64.25.

Some platforms cost nothing at very small volumes. Zeffy charges registered nonprofits nothing and asks buyers for a voluntary tip, and Event Schedule's free plan allows 25 paid tickets a month. The fee calculator works out the cost for your own ticket numbers.

question: Why does Chobble charge a flat fee instead of per-ticket commission?
answer:
Running a ticket site is the same work whatever the tickets cost. Hosting, updates, backups and support do not cost more when an event sells £50 tickets instead of £5 tickets, so the price does not change either.

A commission ties a platform's income to the size of its customers' sales, so the platform earns more by raising its percentage or adding booking fees. A flat fee leaves Chobble's income resting on one thing: whether organisers choose to pay for another term. That keeps the incentive on running a service worth renewing.

Payment providers still charge their own fees. The worked pricing examples compare the totals.

question: Is there a discount for charities or community groups?
answer: Charities, community groups, artists, and musicians get a 50% discount on managed hosting. They pay £25/year on annual billing or £2.50/month on monthly billing. There is no Chobble per-ticket platform fee on either plan. You can sign up for managed hosting, or run the AGPL-3.0-only software on infrastructure you pay for and manage.

question: Can I pay monthly instead of annually?
answer: Yes. Managed hosting costs £5 for a month or £50 for a year, and you pay before each term starts. Twelve months paid one at a time come to £60, which is £10 more than a year paid at once, to cover the extra card fees and admin of twelve payments instead of one. A month does not renew by itself, so there is no plan to cancel: when it ends, you choose whether to pay for another month, a year, or nothing, in which case the site becomes read-only. Charities, community groups, artists and musicians pay half on either term, which is £2.50 a month or £25 a year.

question: Is Chobble Tickets a subscription?
answer: No. Chobble Tickets uses prepay hosting, not subscription billing. You pay for a month or a year in advance, and Chobble does not store card details for automatic renewal. Nothing is charged unless you return and pay for another term. The first prepay month costs £5, or £50 for a year (£25/year or £2.50/month for charities, community groups, artists and musicians). Read how it works on the prepay hosting page.

question: What happens if I stop paying for Chobble Tickets?
answer:
When the paid term ends, the site goes into read-only mode. Nobody can create new events, bookings or attendees, through the admin area or the public site. Existing tickets keep working: attendees can open their confirmation page, show their QR code at the door, and add a pass to Apple or Google Wallet.

You can still log in, view every record, export attendee lists as CSV and download a full database backup. Read-only mode lasts 24 months, Chobble sends reminders during that time, and no payment is owed for those months. Paying for a new term at any point returns the site to normal.

After 24 months in read-only mode, the site and its database are deleted permanently, and any remaining encrypted backup is removed 30 days later. The prepay hosting page explains the billing model.

question: When do I receive the money from ticket sales?
answer: Ticket money goes straight from the buyer to your own Stripe, Square or SumUp account. Chobble never holds it and takes no share of it. Your payment provider decides when it pays out to your bank, and its dashboard shows the payout schedule.

question: Is my attendee data safe?
answer:
Chobble Tickets encrypts attendees' personal details before saving them. Names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, payment identifiers and free-text answers are stored in a form that only your keyed admin accounts can unlock. Someone who copied the database would see only unreadable text.

Each admin user has their own login. Passwords are protected with PBKDF2 at 600,000 iterations, which makes them slow to guess, login attempts are rate limited, and login sessions end after 24 hours. The encryption uses RSA-OAEP with AES-256-GCM, and the encryption page explains how it works.

question: Can Chobble read my attendees' personal information?
answer:
Not in normal use. Attendee details are stored encrypted, Chobble staff do not receive the passwords to organisers' accounts, and the server unlocks the data only while one of your keyed users is signed in. The key is discarded when that session ends.

Chobble can read the data in two cases: if you give Chobble its own login, or if you enable a recovery owner. A recovery owner's credentials are emailed to the recovery address set by the host, and on managed hosting Chobble is the host.

Chobble runs the servers for managed sites, so organisers rely on it running the published code. An organiser who does not want to rely on that can self-host, and Chobble then has no operational access unless the operator grants it.

question: Does Chobble market to my attendees?
answer: No. Managed hosting stores the encrypted booking records that organisers collect, but Chobble does not use those records to build audience profiles, advertise, or market other events. Attendees do not need a Chobble account, are not prompted to download an app, and are not added to a Chobble mailing list. Read more on the no attendee marketing page.

question: Who owns the attendee data?
answer: The organiser is the data controller. Chobble does not claim rights to attendee data or use it for advertising, audience profiles, or product analytics. A payment or email provider processes the details needed when the organiser enables that service. Organisers can export attendee records as CSV and set retention controls.

question: What happens if I lose my admin password?
answer: Without another keyed owner or an enabled recovery owner, losing the last keyed administrator password makes the encrypted attendee data inaccessible. A password reset cannot recreate the private key protected by that password. To avoid this, add a second keyed owner or enable a recovery owner before taking bookings.

question: Is Chobble Tickets hosted in the EU?
answer: The ticketing databases and their backups are held only in Europe. Chobble managed hosting runs on Bunny.net, a company headquartered in Slovenia, and each site's database is kept in the Ireland region of Turso, a US company. Backups are stored with Hetzner in Germany and Scaleway in France. Optional providers may also process data elsewhere. A self-hosted operator can choose another database arrangement. Read the provider breakdown on the hosting locations and data page.

question: Is Chobble affected by the US CLOUD Act?
answer: Chobble CIC is a UK company and Bunny is headquartered in Slovenia. The managed databases sit in Turso's Ireland region, but Turso's operator ChiselStrike Inc. is a US company and subject to US law, including the CLOUD Act. Optional payment, email and integration providers also operate in several jurisdictions. Organisers with specific legal requirements should review each provider before enabling it. The hosting locations and data page lists the main providers and regions.

question: Why is Chobble Tickets open source?
answer:
Chobble's view is that a real alternative to Ticketmaster and the other large platforms has to commit to several things at once, and open source is one of them. The source code is published under AGPL-3.0-only, so anyone can read, run and change it. Anyone who offers a changed version as an online service must publish their changes too.

Chobble is a community interest company with an asset lock and no shareholders, so the code cannot be sold to a private owner. Every site is white-labelled under the organiser's own name and domain, with no shared marketplace. Because anyone can host the software, no single company sits between every organiser and their attendees.

Each of these on its own can be undone or worked around. An open licence does not stop the copyright holder closing future versions, and a company without an asset lock can be sold. Together they remove what the decline Cory Doctorow calls enshittification depends on: an exit that is costly for organisers, and an owner who can be paid out at the end.

Why Chobble Tickets cannot go closed source sets out each protection.

question: Can I self-host Chobble Tickets?
answer: Yes. Chobble charges no software licence fee for self-hosting, while the operator pays for infrastructure and configured services. Supported approaches include Bunny Edge, Deno Deploy and Docker-capable hosts. The recommended Bunny approach uses a fork of the GitHub repository and deploys through GitHub Actions. Read more on the hosting page.

question: Is self-hosting difficult?
answer:
It needs some technical confidence but no programming. The recommended route has five documented steps: fork the GitHub repository, create a Bunny database, create a Bunny edge script linked to the fork, add its secrets in the Bunny dashboard, and add two secrets to the GitHub repository so updates deploy automatically. Docker and other Deno hosts also work, but the operator then keeps the server and database running.

Once the site is live, the operator is responsible for updates, backups and fixing problems. The repository publishes the instructions a coding agent needs, so an agent can carry out the deployment. Managed hosting is there for organisers who would rather not do any of this.

question: What happens to my ticketing if Chobble shuts down?
answer:
The software carries on. The code is published under AGPL-3.0-only, so anyone can run it, and Chobble CIC's asset lock restricts how its assets can be transferred, including if the company is wound up. Self-hosted sites do not depend on Chobble at all.

A managed-hosting organiser can download a full database backup at any time, and the backup restores onto another host with one command. Event setup can also be exported as versioned JSON and imported into any other Chobble Tickets site. A site on the organiser's own domain can point that domain at the new host and keep the same web address.

question: Can I switch away from Chobble Tickets?
answer:
Yes. There is no contract and no exit fee, and a prepaid term ends on its own if you do not renew it. Before leaving, you can export attendee lists as CSV, download the whole database, and export events as versioned JSON.

The CSV files open in any spreadsheet, so the records can go to any other platform. The database backup and JSON exports load into another Chobble Tickets host, including one you run yourself. A site on your own domain can move without changing the address attendees already have.

question: What is a community interest company?
answer: A community interest company (CIC) is a UK company structure for organisations that work for community benefit. Chobble CIC, company number 17050113, is limited by guarantee without share capital and has an asset lock. It reports on its community benefit activities. Chobble receives income from managed hosting and technical work rather than advertising or attendee data sales. Because it has no shareholders, nobody can be paid out by selling the company or closing its software.

question: Can I use my own domain name?
answer: Yes. On managed hosting, you get an instant subdomain (yourname.tix.chobble.net) from day one, and you can add your own custom domain at any time. Up to three URLs can be active at the same time. If you self-host, you control the domain entirely.

question: Can I send emails from my own domain?
answer: Yes. Chobble Tickets supports five email providers: Resend, Postmark, SendGrid, Mailgun (US) and Mailgun (EU). You configure your own account with one of these providers, and confirmation emails are sent from your domain with your branding. Email templates are customisable using Liquid syntax, with built-in filters for formatting currencies and pluralisation.

question: How customisable is Chobble Tickets?
answer: You can customise the header image, the website title and a light or dark theme from the admin area, and change colours and fonts with custom CSS. Email templates use Liquid syntax so you can change the subject line, HTML body, and plain text body of confirmation emails. Event descriptions support Markdown formatting. You can set custom thank-you URLs, configure terms and conditions, and add custom questions, multiple-choice or free text, to the checkout form. If you self-host, you can modify the source code.

question: Does Chobble Tickets support recurring or daily events?
answer: Yes. Daily events have per-date capacity with a calendar date picker, so attendees choose which date they want to attend. You can set holiday and blackout dates to block bookings on specific days. A recurring event, such as a weekly quiz, is one daily listing with its bookable days set to the days it runs, so every week is sold from the same listing.

question: Can I sell different ticket tiers like VIP and general admission?
answer: Yes, using event groups. You create separate events for each tier and group them together. Groups can share capacity, so a confirmed VIP booking reduces the number of general admission tickets available. Attendees see all the options in a single checkout. This also works for early bird and standard pricing, or adult and child tickets.

question: How do QR code check-ins work?
answer: Each booking gets a unique URL with a QR code, which can represent several admissions. Attendees receive it in their confirmation email and can add it to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet. Authorised staff scan the code in a browser with a phone camera. If the connection drops, the scanner queues each scan and checks it in when the connection returns. The scanner warns about previous check-ins and bookings for a different event.

question: Do I need an app to sell tickets or check people in?
answer: No. Chobble Tickets runs in a web browser. The pages are simple, low-bandwidth HTML, so tickets still load on weak signal in a field or a basement. Attendees book through your site without an account or an app download. Their confirmation email carries the ticket link and QR code, and the ticket page has Apple and Google Wallet buttons. Door staff scan tickets through a browser with a phone camera, and the admin panel works in a mobile browser too. Chobble Tickets publishes no consumer app and no organiser mobile app. See the QR code check-ins page.

question: What payment providers does Chobble Tickets support?
answer: Chobble Tickets supports Stripe, Square, and SumUp, with one active card provider per site. You enter the provider credentials in the admin settings. Listings can use fixed prices or pay-what-you-want pricing, and free events need no payment setup. Full refunds can be issued for one booking or in bulk from the admin area, and partial refunds are made in the payment provider's own dashboard.

question: Can I integrate Chobble Tickets with other tools?
answer: Yes. Chobble Tickets has a public JSON API for event listings and booking (no authentication required), an admin API with HMAC-secured keys for full event management, and webhooks that send a POST request on every booking. Webhooks can connect to Slack, Zapier, CRMs, or any service that accepts HTTP requests. There are also ICS calendar feeds and RSS feeds for event listings.

question: Can I collect custom information from attendees at checkout?
answer: Yes. Custom questions can be multiple-choice or free text. This supports meal preferences, clothing sizes, transport choices, access requirements, and other information needed for the event. Answers appear in administration views, CSV exports, and webhook payloads. For multi-event group bookings, the same question is only asked once.

question: Can I set capacity limits for events?
answer: Yes. Each event has a capacity set by the organiser. Chobble Tickets checks capacity before checkout, but this does not reserve anything or use capacity. For a paid booking, capacity is checked again and used only when payment confirmation arrives. An unpaid checkout stops taking payment after one hour, which stops a stale link from paying an old price against changed stock; a fresh checkout re-derives the price and availability, and the window reserves nothing. If two payments race for the last ticket, the later one is refunded automatically and recorded for the organiser. When an event is full, the booking form shows a sold-out message. The checks are a best effort rather than a guarantee against software or infrastructure failures. Daily events have separate capacity for each date, with holiday and blackout dates.

question: Can I embed ticket sales on my own website?
answer: Yes. The embeddable widget adds your event listings to any website with a single line of HTML. The iframe automatically resizes to fit the content. Content Security Policy headers are configurable, so you can control which domains are allowed to embed your booking pages. If you prefer to build your own integration, the public JSON API is available with no authentication required.

question: What features does Chobble Tickets not have?
answer: Chobble Tickets does not have an event discovery marketplace, social media advertising tools, reserved seating with venue maps, waitlists, multi-currency support, virtual event hosting, an organiser mobile app, or telephone support. It includes emailing for existing attendees and promo codes, discounts and add-ons. Organisers who need discovery or venue seating may be better served by another platform; the Eventbrite comparison gives one example.

question: Who runs Chobble Tickets?
answer: Chobble Tickets is built and run by Stefan Burke, who has worked in software and web technology since around 2007. He spent five years at Bandcamp and ten years as the lead developer at Bouncy Castle Network. Stef began trading as Chobble in 2024. Chobble CIC was incorporated on 24 February 2026 as Community Interest Company 17050113. Read more on the About page.

question: Where is Chobble Tickets based?
answer: Chobble CIC is registered in England with its office at 27 The Crescent, Prestwich, Manchester M25 1FL. The platform runs on Bunny.net, headquartered in Slovenia, with databases in the Ireland region of Turso, a US company. Read more about hosting locations on the European page, and more about the company on the about page.

question: Can Chobble Tickets handle equipment hire and deliveries?
answer:
Yes. Listings can span consecutive days with a total price for each offered duration. For a paid booking, capacity across every occupied date is checked and used when payment confirmation arrives. Administrators can assign drop-off and collection work, and logistics agents receive a browser-based run sheet.

See the logistics, multi-day hire, and servicing events pages, or the equipment hire page.

question: Can customers pay a deposit and settle the balance later?
answer:
Yes. Once the deposit payment is confirmed, Chobble Tickets creates the reserved booking and uses capacity. The customer receives a link to a balance page where they can pay the rest later. Payments taken outside the checkout, such as cash or bank transfer, can be recorded against the same balance.

See the deposits and balance payments page.

question: Can Chobble Tickets sell bundles or packages?
answer:
Yes. A group of listings can be sold as a package with a single price, booked together in one checkout. Package members can have fixed quantities and their own price overrides.

See the packages page.

question: Can bookings be taken from an existing website?
answer:
Yes, in two ways. An iframe snippet shows listings inline on any page, and a single JavaScript file turns links on an existing website into add-to-cart buttons with a floating cart.

See the embeddable widget and order widget pages.
